titleStmt.title: Neuronal sensitivity to the interaural time difference of the sound envelope in the mouse inferior colliculus
titleStmt.author: Ono
Bishop
Oliver

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Neuronal sensitivity to the interaural time difference of the sound envelope in the mouse inferior colliculus

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether neurons in the mouse midbrain are sensitive to a binaural timing cue the animal is thought unable to use
span.quote: We examined the sensitivity of the neurons in the mouse inferior colliculus (IC) to the interaural time differences (ITD) conveyed in the sound envelope. Utilizing optogenetic methods, we compared the responses to the ITD in the envelope of identified glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons. More than half of both cell types were sensitive to the envelope ITD, and the ITD curves were aligned at their troughs.

span.label: how neurons respond to interaural time differences carried in the envelope of amplitude-modulated sound, in a small mammal
span.quote: However, the neuronal response to the ITD in the envelope of AM sounds more typical of natural sounds or communication sounds remains to be studied in small mammals.

span.label: the circuitry to process interaural time differences persists in the mouse despite its lack of low-frequency hearing, and is probably shaped in the lateral superior olive
span.quote: These results show that the circuitry to process ITD persists in the mouse despite its lack of low-frequency hearing. The sensitivity of IC neurons to ITD is most likely to be shaped by the binaural interaction of excitation and inhibition in the lateral superior olive.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The present results demonstrated that over half of the neurons in the mouse IC respond an ITD in the envelope of a high-frequency sound.

span.label: envelope interaural time difference sensitivity in inferior colliculus neurons
span.quote: We examined the sensitivity of the neurons in the mouse inferior colliculus (IC) to the interaural time differences (ITD) conveyed in the sound envelope.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Briefly, single cell extracellular recordings were obtained using borosilicate glass pipettes filled with 0.01M phosphate buffered saline (pH 7.4) with 2 % Neurobiotin (4 – 7 MΩ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: It is more likely that ITD-sensitivity in the IC is inherited from the response properties of the neurons in the brainstem.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Thus, the ITD sensitivity of neurons in the mouse IC is most likely to be due to inputs from the LSO.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The IC neurons might inherit this response property from contralateral LSO neurons because the contralateral projections from LSO neurons are exclusively excitatory

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The trough-type ITD sensitivity is suggested to be shaped by the coincidence of bilateral excitatory-inhibitory synaptic inputs

span.label: the sensitivity is probably not built in the midbrain but inherited from the brainstem
span.quote: It is more likely that ITD-sensitivity in the IC is inherited from the response properties of the neurons in the brainstem.

span.label: the lateral superior olive is much larger than the medial superior olive in the mouse, which is the argument for it being the source
span.quote: Anatomical observations show that the LSO is much larger than MSO in the mouse ( Fischl et al., 2016 ; Ito et al., 2011 ). Thus, the ITD sensitivity of neurons in the mouse IC is most likely to be due to inputs from the LSO.

span.label: contralateral projections from the lateral superior olive are exclusively excitatory while ipsilateral ones are mixed, which would explain why firing rises when the contralateral sound leads
span.quote: The IC neurons might inherit this response property from contralateral LSO neurons because the contralateral projections from LSO neurons are exclusively excitatory ( Oliver et al., 1995 ). In contrast, the ipsilateral projections from LSO neurons are both excitatory and inhibitory ( Oliver et al., 1995 ). Thus, the inputs from the ipsilateral LSO might be balanced and have a smaller effect on the IC neurons.

span.label: GABAergic cells may not carry the timing information themselves but could sharpen tuning downstream by raising conductance
span.quote: Even though the inhibition from the GABAergic IC neuron may not convey ITD information, it might increase the conductance in the postsynaptic neurons ( Funabiki et al., 1998 ) and sharpen the ITD tuning via ‘iceberg effect’

span.label: lateral superior olive neurons in gerbil change firing probability over microseconds, so even a small mammal with an undeveloped medial superior olive could detect these differences
span.quote: The LSO neurons in gerbil varied their firing probability when the ITD changed in the order of microseconds ( Beiderbeck et al., 2018 ). This suggested that the LSO could detect ITD as well as ILD. So, even small mammals with an undeveloped MSO might be able to detect ITD via LSO neurons.

span.label: Only a limited stimulus set was tested, so the reported proportion of ITD-sensitive neurons may be an underestimate.
span.quote: Furthermore, it is possible that even more neurons in the mouse IC might turn out to be sensitive to envelope ITD if they are tested with more diverse sound stimuli than those used in the present study.

span.label: Best and characteristic frequency could not be determined for two glutamatergic cells.
span.quote: In two glutamatergic neurons, we could not identify either BF or CF because their responsiveness to tones was too low.

span.label: The raised-sine stimulus broadens the carrier spectrum, which could itself affect measured ITD sensitivity.
span.quote: Since the spectrum width of the carrier noise was shown to affect the sensitivity of the envelope ITD in LSO neurons, the broadening of the spectrum in the raised sine stimuli might affect the ITD sensitivity in the IC neurons.

span.label: the neuronal mechanism behind the dependence on envelope shape is stated to be unknown
span.quote: It is unclear what neuronal mechanism underlies this sensitivity to the envelope shape.

span.label: more neurons might prove sensitive if tested with a wider range of stimuli than were used here
span.quote: Furthermore, it is possible that even more neurons in the mouse IC might turn out to be sensitive to envelope ITD if they are tested with more diverse sound stimuli than those used in the present study.

span.label: the spectral-broadening artefact of the raised sine stimulus is bounded at under 10 percent, but the supporting measurement is not shown
span.quote: Since the spectrum width of the carrier noise was shown to affect the sensitivity of the envelope ITD in LSO neurons, the broadening of the spectrum in the raised sine stimuli might affect the ITD sensitivity in the IC neurons. To validate the effect, we measured the spectrum of modeled waveforms and found that the raised sine stimuli had a broader spectrum band than one-octave noise as the modulation frequency increased. However, the broadening of the spectrum band was less than 10% even at a modulation frequency of 512 Hz when the roll-off factor was 16 (data not shown). So, the effect of the spectrum change is likely to be limited.

span.label: recordings were dropped when the recording depth and the labelled site did not clearly correspond
span.quote: We excluded the data when the correspondence between the recording depth and the labeled site was ambiguous.

span.label: the change in firing rate within the mouse's own physiological range was very small, so the authors conclude the cue may have minimal effect
span.quote: The present data shows that the most IC neurons increased their firing when the contralateral sound preceded the ipsilateral sound. However, the change in firing rate within physiological ITD range was very small in most neurons ( Fig. 6 ). So, the ITD may have minimal effects on the firing rate of the IC neurons.

span.label: the raised-sine envelope, imported because a listener's threshold is lower for it than for a sinusoid
span.quote: The raised sine AM sound contains more spectral sidebands than SAM ( Bernstein et al., 2009 ) as does any sound with a rapid rise time.

span.label: CP as an index of alignment, where 0 means the ITD curves are aligned near their peaks and 0.5 near their troughs
span.quote: CP is the index of the alignment: A CP of 0 indicates that the ITD curves are aligned near their peaks, while a CP of 0.5 indicates that the ITD curves are aligned near their troughs

span.label: ITD here means the delay between the ENVELOPES, not between the fine structures - the stimulus is built so the carrier has no interaural phase difference at all, which is what makes the claim possible in a high-frequency animal
span.quote: The noise had the same waveform with the same phase in both ears. Thus, there was no phase difference in the noise delivered to both ears. Consequently, in the binaural beat AM sound that we used, ITD was only generated in the envelope, and not in the fine sound structure.

span.label: GABAergic here means a cell the light drove, and glutamatergic a cell the light suppressed by more than 50 percent - a class defined by a response threshold, validated separately against GAD67 staining
span.quote: Light evoked firing in GABAergic neurons but suppressed spikes in other neurons. We judged that the neuron was suppressed when the light reduced sound evoked spikes by more than 50%. We verified the validity of the optogenetic identification by immunohistochemical identification of GAD67

span.label: CP is an index whose two values ARE the two hypotheses: 0 means the curves align at peaks, 0.5 means they align at troughs, so the measurement returns the answer directly rather than a test statistic
span.quote: CP is the index of the alignment: A CP of 0 indicates that the ITD curves are aligned near their peaks, while a CP of 0.5 indicates that the ITD curves are aligned near their troughs

span.label: the physiological ITD range of the mouse is a derived quantity, from head size, and it is what makes every result here a claim about a cue the animal may never encounter
span.quote: Small animals, including mice, have a small head size and are thought to have only a small physiological range of ITD (e.g. ±50 μs in mice; Allen et al., 2010 ). Instead, small animals use interaural level difference (ILD) as the predominant cue for sound localization.

span.label: an animal is included only if its auditory brainstem response threshold is under 40 dB - hearing is an inclusion criterion with a number, not an assumption
span.quote: After the craniotomy, the auditory brainstem response (ABR) to a click (0.5 ms) was measured to verify normal hearing. The threshold of the ABR was (left, 30.7 ± 1.1 dB, right, 30.3 ± 1.0 dB, n = 30). Mice were used for experiments only when the ABR threshold was less than 40 dB.

span.label: builds-on → Ono et al., 2016; Ono et al., 2017 (optogenetic cell-type identification in IC)
span.quote: As shown in our previous studies, the laser-light stimulation of the IC evoked firing in GABAergic and inhibited firing in glutamatergic neurons ( Ono et al., 2016 ; Ono et al., 2017 ).

span.label: extends → Ono et al., 2017 (pure-tone response properties of IC cell types)
span.quote: Our previous study showed that GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons shared similar response properties to pure tones ( Ono et al., 2017 ).

span.label: builds-on → Batra et al., 1997c; Joris et al., 1995 (LSO envelope-ITD sensitivity in cat and rabbit)
span.quote: Supporting this view, the previous studies in the cat and rabbit showed that the neurons in LSO could detect the envelope ITDs and had a trough-type ITD sensitivity ( Batra et al., 1997c ; Joris et al., 1995 ).

span.label: builds-on → Bernstein et al., 1985 (human psychophysics of envelope ITD)
span.quote: This is consistent with previous psychophysics observations that a large envelope ITD was necessary to produce a shift of the intracranial acoustic image away from the midline ( Bernstein et al., 1985 ).

span.label: extends → reports that envelope interaural time differences are detected in the lateral superior olive of cat and rabbit
span.quote: Anatomical observations show that the LSO is much larger than MSO in the mouse ( Fischl et al., 2016 ; Ito et al., 2011 ). Thus, the ITD sensitivity of neurons in the mouse IC is most likely to be due to inputs from the LSO.

span.label: qualifies → the behavioural finding that mice cannot use interaural time differences in low-frequency sound to localise
span.quote: In line with this, small mammals such as mice and rats only hear high frequency sounds which generate larger ILDs than low frequency sounds ( Grothe et al., 2014 ), and it has been reported that they could not utilize ITD in low-frequency sounds as a sound localization cue

span.label: supports → the proposal that a vestigial binaural circuit can persist in an animal that no longer uses it, as discussed for the Mexican free-tailed bat
span.quote: It is possible that ITD sensitivity to the neural envelope in IC is part of a neuronal circuit that is no longer used by mice for binaural hearing, similar to that discussed for the Mexican free-tailed bat

span.label: confirms → psychophysical observations that a large envelope ITD is needed to shift the intracranial image away from the midline
span.quote: This is consistent with previous psychophysics observations that a large envelope ITD was necessary to produce a shift of the intracranial acoustic image away from the midline

span.label: builds-on → the peak-type and trough-type classification of ITD sensitivity established in the rabbit inferior colliculus
span.quote: Previous studies reported that two types of ITD sensitivity were observed in the IC of the rabbit: peak-type and trough-type ( Batra et al., 1993 ). In the trough type neurons, the ITD curves are aligned at troughs ( Fig. 1C , D , 5A , B ) to produce a composite (average ITD) curve with a distinct trough. The ITD curves in the peak-type neuron are aligned at peaks

span.label: ITD —contrasted-with→ ILD
span.quote: Small animals, including mice, have a small head size and are thought to have only a small physiological range of ITD (e.g. ±50 μs in mice; Allen et al., 2010 ). Instead, small animals use interaural level difference (ILD) as the predominant cue for sound localization.

span.label: envelope —operationalised-as→ ITD
span.quote: The noise had the same waveform with the same phase in both ears. Thus, there was no phase difference in the noise delivered to both ears. Consequently, in the binaural beat AM sound that we used, ITD was only generated in the envelope, and not in the fine sound structure.

span.label: LSO —contrasted-with→ MSO
span.quote: Anatomical observations show that the LSO is much larger than MSO in the mouse ( Fischl et al., 2016 ; Ito et al., 2011 ). Thus, the ITD sensitivity of neurons in the mouse IC is most likely to be due to inputs from the LSO.

span.label: LSO —causes→ IC
span.quote: Anatomical observations show that the LSO is much larger than MSO in the mouse ( Fischl et al., 2016 ; Ito et al., 2011 ). Thus, the ITD sensitivity of neurons in the mouse IC is most likely to be due to inputs from the LSO.

span.label: lateral lemniscus —causes→ IC
span.quote: Besides LSO, the nuclei of the lateral lemniscus may contribute to binaural processing in the IC.

span.label: MGB —causes→ IC
span.quote: The role of ITD-sensitive glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons in the IC may depend on their interaction in neurons postsynaptic to IC inputs, for example in the medial geniculate body (MGB).

span.label: ICC —part-of→ IC
span.quote: ITD-sensitive neurons were found in the central nucleus of IC (ICC) in three regions: glycine-rich Area 1, GABA-rich Area 2 and the border of Area 1 and 2

span.label: GABAergic —contrasted-with→ glutamatergic
span.quote: The IC consists of glutamatergic (75 %) and GABAergic neurons (25%). In the central sensory pathways, the interaction of excitation and inhibition is known to be critical in shaping the neural responses; however, it is not known to what extent these neuron types process ITD.

span.label: ChR2 —operationalised-as→ GABAergic
span.quote: To distinguish the glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons in in vivo recordings, we used transgenic mice (VGAT-ChR2 mice) in which the inhibitory neurons specifically express channelrhodopsin2 ( Zhao et al., 2011 ). As shown in our previous studies, the laser-light stimulation of the IC evoked firing in GABAergic and inhibited firing in glutamatergic neurons

span.label: GAD67 —operationalised-as→ GABAergic
span.quote: Light evoked firing in GABAergic neurons but suppressed spikes in other neurons. We judged that the neuron was suppressed when the light reduced sound evoked spikes by more than 50%. We verified the validity of the optogenetic identification by immunohistochemical identification of GAD67

span.label: CP —operationalised-as→ trough-type
span.quote: In the both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons, CPs were close to 0.5 ( Fig. 5E - G ), both to SAM (GABA, 0.46 ± 0.02, n =5, GLU, 0.50 ± 0.01, n = 9) and raised sine stimuli (GABA, 0.41, n = 1, GLU, 0.46 ± 0.03). This observation is consistent with the trough-type response of most neurons in the mouse IC.

span.label: trough-type —contrasted-with→ peak-type
span.quote: Previous studies reported that two types of ITD sensitivity were observed in the IC of the rabbit: peak-type and trough-type ( Batra et al., 1993 ). In the trough type neurons, the ITD curves are aligned at troughs ( Fig. 1C , D , 5A , B ) to produce a composite (average ITD) curve with a distinct trough. The ITD curves in the peak-type neuron are aligned at peaks

span.label: CD —operationalised-as→ ITD
span.quote: The other parameter, CD, gives the common ITD at which maximal excitation or suppression occurs in peak- or trough- type neuron, respectively.

span.label: vector strength —operationalised-as→ ITD
span.quote: To examine how the ITD-sensitive neurons in the IC were synchronized to the beat and monaural modulation frequencies in envelope, we quantified the phase locking of spike responses to sound stimuli by measuring vector strength (VS).

span.label: phase-locking —distinct-from→ IC
span.quote: However, in order to obtain ITD sensitivity initially, it is necessary for the monaural contralateral and ipsilateral synaptic inputs to be highly phase-locked to the envelope. Our results suggest that the phase-locking of IC neurons to monaural sounds may be insufficient to explain the ITD sensitivity. The phase-locking to the monaural contralateral sound degraded in the IC neurons at higher modulation frequencies ( Fig.2C , D ) despite the fact that some IC neurons had ITD-sensitivity to high-frequency modulation. Thus, it is unlikely that the ITD sensitivity to the high-frequency modulation is shaped within the IC itself.

span.label: coincidence detection —distinct-from→ IC
span.quote: These results suggested that the ITD sensitivity to the binaural beat with high modulation frequency was not likely to be shaped by the coincidence detection in the IC neurons.

span.label: ILD —causes→ IC
span.quote: Interestingly, this firing pattern shaped by envelope ITD matches that of the ILD, because in the IC, the ILD also evokes a higher firing rate when the contralateral sound level is more intense than the ipsilateral sound level

span.label: iceberg effect —causes→ GABAergic
span.quote: Even though the inhibition from the GABAergic IC neuron may not convey ITD information, it might increase the conductance in the postsynaptic neurons ( Funabiki et al., 1998 ) and sharpen the ITD tuning via ‘iceberg effect’

span.label: raised sine —contrasted-with→ SAM
span.quote: The raised sine AM sound contains more spectral sidebands than SAM ( Bernstein et al., 2009 ) as does any sound with a rapid rise time.

span.label: Rayleigh test —operationalised-as→ binaural beat
span.quote: ITD sensitivity of the recorded neuron was assessed by testing whether the spike responses to binaural beat AM sound was significantly synchronized to beat frequency (1 Hz). Among the responses whose firing rate was higher than 1 Hz, the synchronization was evaluated by the Rayleigh test

span.label: rMTF —operationalised-as→ modulation frequency
span.quote: We measured the rMTF to binaural beat AM sound to evaluate the change of firing rate relevant to modulation frequency

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Among the responses whose firing rate was higher than 1 Hz, the synchronization was evaluated by the Rayleigh test (p < 0.001)

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The synchronization change with the modulation frequency was significant in the glutamatergic neurons (p = 0.00545, Fisher’s exact test), but not in the GABAergic neurons (p = 0.1892, Fisher’s exact test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The percentages of the neurons synchronized to the beat frequency were not significantly different between glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons (p = 0.0625, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The slope was not significantly different between the GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons, either (P = 0.519, Two-way ANOVA test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: the firing rates of synchronized glutamatergic neurons were significantly higher than the unsynchronized responses of both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons at the modulation frequencies of 64 (P < 0.05, Tukey HSD test)

span.label: statistics
span.quote: To measure the CD and the CP, we plotted the mean interaural phase of the response against the modulation frequency, and fitted the phases with linear regression

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The VS beat and VS contra were hardly or only weakly correlated (SAM-GABA, R = 0.178, n = 25, SAM-GLU, R = 0.208, n = 45, Raised-GABA, R = −0.316, n = 11, Raised-GLU, R = 0.112, n = 33).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: we quantified the phase locking of spike responses to sound stimuli by measuring vector strength (VS)

span.label: statistics
span.quote: ITD sensitivity of the recorded neuron was assessed by testing whether the spike responses to binaural beat AM sound was significantly synchronized to beat frequency (1 Hz). Among the responses whose firing rate was higher than 1 Hz, the synchronization was evaluated by the Rayleigh test

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The percentages of the neurons synchronized to the beat frequency were not significantly different between glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons (p = 0.0625, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The slope was slightly higher, but not significantly so, in the responses to the raised sine (GABA, 15.2 ± 11.3 Hz/ms, n = 12, GLU, 17.7 ± 7.6 Hz/ms, n = 32) as opposed to the SAM (GABA, 4.6 ± 2.6 Hz/ms, n = 27, 9.2 ± 3.5 Hz/ms, n = 47) (P = 0.117, Two-way ANOVA test).

span.label: statistics
span.quote: To examine how the ITD-sensitive neurons in the IC were synchronized to the beat and monaural modulation frequencies in envelope, we quantified the phase locking of spike responses to sound stimuli by measuring vector strength (VS).

span.label: More than half of both inhibitory and excitatory inferior colliculus neurons in the mouse locked their firing to the binaural beat carried in the sound envelope, i.e. they were envelope-ITD sensitive.
span.quote: More than half of both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons showed synchronization to the binaural beat frequency in envelopes

span.label: This is the first demonstration of envelope-ITD sensitivity anywhere in the mouse auditory pathway.
span.quote: To the best of our knowledge, the neural sensitivity to the ITD in the envelope has not been shown in the auditory pathway of the mouse previously.

span.label: The proportion of ITD-sensitive neurons did not differ between glutamatergic and GABAergic cells.
span.quote: The percentages of the neurons synchronized to the beat frequency were not significantly different between glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons (p = 0.0625, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: Characteristic delay coincided with the trough rather than the peak of the ITD curve in most cells, identifying them as trough-type.
span.quote: These results showed that CD was close to trough in the most IC neurons.

span.label: Within the mouse's physiological ITD range the ITD curve slopes positively toward the contralateral side for both cell types, so firing is higher when the contralateral envelope leads.
span.quote: In most ITD curves, the slope of the ITD curve within the physiological ITD range (gray filled square) was positive toward contralateral sides, regardless of the cell type and stimulation type

span.label: Above 256 Hz modulation, phase-locking to the binaural beat exceeded phase-locking to the monaural contralateral stimulus, so the high-frequency ITD sensitivity cannot be built by coincidence detection inside the IC.
span.quote: However, in most responses, the VS contra was smaller than the VS beat when the modulation frequency was higher than 256 Hz.

span.label: Rate modulation transfer functions of most IC neurons of both types fell into the low-rate, low-pass or band-reject classes for sinusoidal modulation.
span.quote: Most neurons were classified as low rate, low pass or band reject in the response to SAM, and this was true for both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons

span.label: Glutamatergic neurons that were synchronized to the beat fired faster than unsynchronized neurons of either type at 64 and 128 Hz modulation.
span.quote: the firing rates of synchronized glutamatergic neurons were significantly higher than the unsynchronized responses of both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons at the modulation frequencies of 64 (P < 0.05, Tukey HSD test)

span.label: The slope of the ITD curve near zero did not differ between GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.
span.quote: The slope was not significantly different between the GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons, either (P = 0.519, Two-way ANOVA test).

span.label: more than half of both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons synchronised to the binaural beat frequency in the envelopes
span.quote: More than half of both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons showed synchronization to the binaural beat frequency in envelopes

span.label: 47 neurons were recorded, 18 GABAergic and 29 glutamatergic
span.quote: We recorded the responses to binaural beat AM sound from 47 neurons, of which 18 were GABAergic and 29 were glutamatergic.

span.label: characteristic phase was close to 0.5 in both cell types, which is the trough-type pattern
span.quote: In the both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons, CPs were close to 0.5 ( Fig. 5E - G ), both to SAM (GABA, 0.46 ± 0.02, n =5, GLU, 0.50 ± 0.01, n = 9) and raised sine stimuli (GABA, 0.41, n = 1, GLU, 0.46 ± 0.03). This observation is consistent with the trough-type response of most neurons in the mouse IC.

span.label: the squared deviation from the unity line was significantly smaller for mean trough time than mean peak time, 0.87 against 6.62 ms squared
span.quote: To compare the proximity to CD, we calculated the squared deviation of each point from the unity line ( Fig. 5H , dotted line) in the scattered plot of mean trough time and peak time. The squared deviation was significantly smaller in mean trough time than in mean peak time (trough, 0.87 ± 0.38 ms 2 , peak, 6.62 ± 1.31 ms 2 , n= 21, P = 0.00061, Wilcoxon signed rank test).

span.label: within the physiological ITD range the slope was positive toward the contralateral side, whatever the cell type or stimulus
span.quote: In most ITD curves, the slope of the ITD curve within the physiological ITD range (gray filled square) was positive toward contralateral sides, regardless of the cell type and stimulation type

span.label: the same directional pattern holds for level differences in these neurons, so the two cues would add rather than oppose
span.quote: Interestingly, this firing pattern shaped by envelope ITD matches that of the ILD, because in the IC, the ILD also evokes a higher firing rate when the contralateral sound level is more intense than the ipsilateral sound level

span.label: VS contra was larger than VS beat when the modulation frequency was lower than 128 Hz, and smaller than VS beat when it was higher than 256 Hz
span.quote: As was shown in the SOC, the VS contra was larger than the VS beat when the modulation frequency was lower than 128 Hz ( Fig. 2C , D ). However, in most responses, the VS contra was smaller than the VS beat when the modulation frequency was higher than 256 Hz.

span.label: THE LOCAL MECHANISM EXCLUDED BY THE PAPER'S OWN DATA: sensitivity at high modulation frequency is not likely to be shaped by coincidence detection in the IC
span.quote: These results suggested that the ITD sensitivity to the binaural beat with high modulation frequency was not likely to be shaped by the coincidence detection in the IC neurons.

span.label: THE INGREDIENT IS WORSE THAN THE PRODUCT: a local mechanism needs highly phase-locked monaural inputs, and monaural phase-locking degrades where the sensitivity persists
span.quote: However, in order to obtain ITD sensitivity initially, it is necessary for the monaural contralateral and ipsilateral synaptic inputs to be highly phase-locked to the envelope. Our results suggest that the phase-locking of IC neurons to monaural sounds may be insufficient to explain the ITD sensitivity. The phase-locking to the monaural contralateral sound degraded in the IC neurons at higher modulation frequencies ( Fig.2C , D ) despite the fact that some IC neurons had ITD-sensitivity to high-frequency modulation. Thus, it is unlikely that the ITD sensitivity to the high-frequency modulation is shaped within the IC itself.

span.label: so the sensitivity is more likely inherited from brainstem neurons than built in the midbrain
span.quote: It is more likely that ITD-sensitivity in the IC is inherited from the response properties of the neurons in the brainstem.

span.label: ARTEFACT BOUNDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY: the raised sine broadens the spectrum by less than 10 percent even at 512 Hz, so its effect is judged limited
span.quote: Since the spectrum width of the carrier noise was shown to affect the sensitivity of the envelope ITD in LSO neurons, the broadening of the spectrum in the raised sine stimuli might affect the ITD sensitivity in the IC neurons. To validate the effect, we measured the spectrum of modeled waveforms and found that the raised sine stimuli had a broader spectrum band than one-octave noise as the modulation frequency increased. However, the broadening of the spectrum band was less than 10% even at a modulation frequency of 512 Hz when the roll-off factor was 16 (data not shown). So, the effect of the spectrum change is likely to be limited.

span.label: NULL BETWEEN CELL TYPES: the percentages synchronised did not differ significantly between glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons
span.quote: The percentages of the neurons synchronized to the beat frequency were not significantly different between glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons (p = 0.0625, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: NULL AGAIN: fewer GABAergic than glutamatergic neurons synchronised to the raised sine, and that difference was not significant either
span.quote: Fewer GABAergic neurons were synchronized than glutamatergic neurons but this was not a significance difference (p = 0.125, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

span.label: the ITD slope was neither significantly different between envelope shapes nor between cell types
span.quote: The slope was slightly higher, but not significantly so, in the responses to the raised sine (GABA, 15.2 ± 11.3 Hz/ms, n = 12, GLU, 17.7 ± 7.6 Hz/ms, n = 32) as opposed to the SAM (GABA, 4.6 ± 2.6 Hz/ms, n = 27, 9.2 ± 3.5 Hz/ms, n = 47) (P = 0.117, Two-way ANOVA test).

span.label: THE AUTHORS DEFLATE THEIR OWN RESULT: the firing-rate change within the physiological range was very small, so the cue may have minimal effect on these neurons
span.quote: The present data shows that the most IC neurons increased their firing when the contralateral sound preceded the ipsilateral sound. However, the change in firing rate within physiological ITD range was very small in most neurons ( Fig. 6 ). So, the ITD may have minimal effects on the firing rate of the IC neurons.

span.label: AND OFFER A VESTIGIAL READING: the sensitivity may belong to a circuit mice no longer use for binaural hearing
span.quote: It is possible that ITD sensitivity to the neural envelope in IC is part of a neuronal circuit that is no longer used by mice for binaural hearing, similar to that discussed for the Mexican free-tailed bat

span.label: the trough of the ITD curve covers most of the mouse's whole physiological range
span.quote: The small head size of a mouse may limit the “physiological” range of ITD to ±50 μsec, and the trough of the ITD curve covers most of that range.

span.quote: Nevertheless, mice might experience longer ITDs in a natural environment with sound reflections and echoes, and these could drive the LSO neurons.
